match.reason: The new point covers all three ways heat moves, including radiation across empty space, but the bank points only teach conduction and convection, so no single point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Conduction, convection and radiation
card: Conduction
Heat moves through a solid from particle to particle. Hot, fast-vibrating particles pass energy to their cooler neighbours. Metals are good at this.
Convection
Heat moves through a liquid or gas in currents. Warmed fluid spreads out and rises, cooler fluid sinks to take its place, and a loop of moving fluid forms.
Radiation
Heat travels as waves, such as infrared waves. These can cross empty space, so no particles are needed. This is how the Sun warms Earth.
Many everyday cases involve more than one type. A metal spoon in hot soup heats up by conduction, and the soup itself mixes by convection.
draft.remember: Conduction needs touching particles in a solid. Convection needs a moving liquid or gas. Radiation needs neither.

a.q: Heat from the Sun reaches Earth across space. Which type of heat transfer is this?
a.why: Space is almost empty, so there are no particles to pass heat along. Only radiation can cross it. Conduction and convection both need particles.
a.clue: Which type does not need any particles?

b.q: Mia puts a pot of water on a hot stove. The water at the bottom warms, rises and is replaced by cooler water from above. What is this movement of heat called?
b.why: Warmed water rises and cooler water sinks, which makes a current. Heat carried by a current in a liquid is convection. Conduction is tempting because the stove heats the pot, but it passes heat through a solid, not through moving water.
b.clue: Look for a current in a liquid.

problems.detail: 'Conduction needs touching particles in a solid' is stricter than the card and not quite true: conduction also happens in liquids and gases, only more slowly. Students may learn that conduction cannot happen in a fluid. Suggest 'Conduction passes heat between touching particles, best in solids such as metals.'

check.summary: Both questions are correct, with one clear right answer each. The remember line wrongly implies that conduction happens only in solids, when it also happens, more slowly, in liquids and gases.
